question.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 & -9 & 5\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
question.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{11}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 & -9 & 5\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & -8 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & -8 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 5 \\ -8 & -3 & 2 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 5 \\ -8 & -3 & 2 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 9 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(3-45) \\  & =126.\end{aligned}
$$
